definitions.explanation: Foods that have been preserved by drying, such as dried seaweed, dried mushrooms, and dried fish.

examples.japanese: {乾物|かんぶつ}は{長期|ちょうき}{保存|ほぞん}ができる。
examples.english: Dried foods can be stored for a long time.

examples.japanese: {乾物|かんぶつ}を{水|みず}で{戻|もど}してから{料理|りょうり}に{使|つか}う。
examples.english: Rehydrate the dried food in water before using it in cooking.

examples.japanese: {乾物屋|かんぶつや}で{昆布|こんぶ}と{干|ほ}し{椎茸|しいたけ}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought kelp and dried shiitake mushrooms at the dried goods store.

notes:
USAGE: {乾物|かんぶつ} is a collective term for various dried foods that are staples in Japanese cooking.

COMMON EXAMPLES:
・{干|ほ}し{椎茸|しいたけ} - dried shiitake mushrooms
・{昆布|こんぶ} - dried kelp
・{海苔|のり} - dried seaweed (nori)
・{鰹節|かつおぶし} - dried bonito flakes
・{切|き}り{干|ぼ}し{大根|だいこん} - dried daikon radish strips
・{高野豆腐|こうやどうふ} - freeze-dried tofu

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{乾物|かんぶつ}を{戻|もど}す (to rehydrate dried food)
・{乾物屋|かんぶつや} (dried goods store)

CULTURAL NOTE: {乾物|かんぶつ} has been an essential part of Japanese cuisine for centuries, allowing preservation of seasonal ingredients and providing umami flavor to dishes like {出汁|だし}.
